title: Doubling the code bound
statement: Fix $E,B\in\mathbb N$, an oracle on four indices and Boolean strings, an input bit string $x$, a proposition $Q$, and a register state $\sigma$. For every $m\in\mathbb N$ such that $\sigma.e=m$, suppose all seventeen quantities in $\sigma$ are at most $B$, $\sigma.K\,2^m\le B$, and for every $k',T'\le B$ the procedure started in state $\mathrm{st0}$ with $e=0$, $K=\sigma.K\,2^m$, $k=k'$, and $T=T'$ terminates with all registers at most $B$ and accepts if and only if $Q$ holds. Then the procedure started in state $\mathrm{db}$ with state $\sigma$ terminates with all registers at most $B$ and accepts if and only if $Q$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: oracle on four indices and Boolean strings
all seventeen quantities in $\sigma$ are at most $B$

replaced:
Let $Q$ be a proposition, let $E,B\in\mathbb N$, and fix the oracle, input, and register
bound defining the generator semantics. For every $m\in\mathbb N$ and register state
$\sigma$ with exponent register $e=m$, suppose every register of $\sigma$ is at most
$B$, $K\,2^m\le B$, and, for every $k',T'\le B$, the generator starting in its
counting-initialization state with exponent $0$, code bound $K\,2^m$, and scratch
registers $k',T'$ terminates with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when
$Q$ holds. Then the generator starting in its doubling state at $\sigma$ also terminates
with all registers bounded by $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds.
